explanation: In Spain, patting someone on the head is typically reserved for children or very close family members; doing so to an adult, even in a friendly social gathering, can be perceived as condescending or invasive of personal space. Spanish culture values personal autonomy and physical boundaries, and head-patting is often associated with treating someone like a child or pet.
local_tip: Avoid patting anyone on the head in Spain; instead, offer a light touch on the arm or shoulder to show friendliness.
regional_note: In some rural areas of Andalusia or Catalonia, older generations may be more tolerant of head pats from close friends, but it remains uncommon.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred body part in Thai culture, and touching it is highly disrespectful.
Patting the head is acceptable for children but can be seen as patronizing for adults; avoid with strangers or elders.
